conviction_note: Findings net to about -1.0 point (forward wafer commitments cut a third against a supply-hoarding story management told, partly offset by an unguided one-off R&D credit and a live never-denied bid); I add roughly -3 more by partially weighting a brutal reaction base rate (5 of 7 down, mean -9.2%, last three -15% to -21%), discounted heavily because 20 points of run-in are already spent and a reported >$3bn strategic bidder damps the left tail.

findings.finding: Ambarella cut total manufacturing purchase commitments 33% sequentially, from $80.4m at 31-Jan-26 to $53.9m at 30-Apr-26, and booked a first-ever $1.2m adverse-purchase-commitment loss liability (it was exactly $0 the prior quarter) - while inventory rose 54% to $80.4m and days of inventory went 99 to 145, a build management told the call was precautionary against a second-half supply shortage.
findings.why_not_priced: The two facts point opposite ways and only one of them is visible in any aggregator. Inventory and days-of-inventory are screened fields and management gave them a benign supply-insurance framing on the call; the forward commitment balance is a hand-tagged XBRL item in a commitments footnote that no data vendor carries, and it contradicts that framing - you do not cut your forward wafer book by a third if you fear a shortage, and you do not accrue for adverse commitments unless your demand forecast has fallen below your committed supply. If the market had read it, the sell side would not be sitting at a $95 consensus target with Rosenblatt at $120 and an all-Buy tape on 2026-08-31, and the stock would not have risen 38% from $62.13 on 26-Jun to $86.00 on 31-Jul on broker-note and M&A narrative in the eight weeks AFTER this 10-Q was public. The August drawdown is also not this: it tracks a merger-premium unwind plus SOXX, so the fundamental signal is unspent.
findings.independence: Different document, same reporting event: the Q1 call transcript is where management supplies both the 99-to-145 days figure and the supply-shortage rationale that the commitment book contradicts - https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/ambarella-amba-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/ (2026-05-28). Separately corroborating the margin channel, contemporaneous filing coverage records Q1 GAAP gross margin falling to 58.4% from 60.0% explicitly 'attributed to higher manufacturing costs and adverse purchase commitments', plus operating cash flow of negative $25.6m on the inventory investment - https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/AMBA/10-q-ambarella-inc-quarterly-earnings-report-d5da44c5577f.html (2026-06-02). NOTE: the commitments and adverse-accrual numbers themselves come from the same 10-Q as finding 2, so treat the two findings as one source cluster.

findings.finding: A customer development project funded by a $13.5m cash advance was terminated on 12-May-26; $4.5m is refunded and the remaining $9.0m is XBRL-tagged as a forecast reduction of R&D expense in the quarter ended 31-Jul-26 - i.e. tonight's quarter - yet the 28-May press release and the earnings call both omitted it entirely while guiding Q2 non-GAAP opex to $56.0-59.0m against $56.4m actual in Q1.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic forces a fork the five models on this name cannot both have taken, and consensus reconciles to the naive branch. R&D is roughly four-fifths of Ambarella's opex, so a $9.0m credit is a ~20% cut to the R&D line; for reported non-GAAP opex still to land inside $56-59m the underlying run-rate would have to have jumped ~16% sequentially with zero explanation given. Consensus of a ($0.30) GAAP loss on 5 estimates bridges almost exactly off the $56-59m guide midpoint at face value, which is what you get when analysts take the guide and never open the footnote. So either the credit sits on top of the guide as an unguided ~$0.21/share benefit, or it is silently inside it and Q3 opex must step back up ~$9m - and management has said nothing that lets the market tell which. Had this been priced, at least one of the press release, the prepared remarks or the Q&A would have carried the words 'one-time' or 'credit', and none does.
findings.independence: The non-disclosure is established by two documents separate from the 10-Q: the 28-May-26 results release, which mentions no terminated project, no deposit and neither the $13.5m nor the $9.0m - https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/28/3303255/23306/en/ambarella-inc-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results.html - and the full call transcript, in which none of those terms appears anywhere while Fermi Wang was simultaneously selling the LTA/NRE pipeline ('most of the discussion will involve NRE') - https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/ambarella-amba-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/. Partly against me: retail filing coverage did surface the item on 2026-06-02 (stocktitan, URL in finding 1), so it is not wholly uncovered. Shares the 10-Q source cluster with finding 1.

findings.finding: The stock at $65.43 is 5.4% BELOW its pre-rumour close of $69.19 on 29-Jul-26, i.e. the entire premium from the FT's 31-Jul-26 report that NXP was in talks to buy the company for over $3bn has been erased and then some, with no report anywhere that the talks collapsed - and the -20.1% 20-session slide compares with only -6.8% for SOXX over the same span, so ~13 points of it is idiosyncratic and unattributed to any dated company news.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about the shape of the distribution, not a private fact, and it is the reason I am not simply stacking the -9.2% mean reaction on top of my negative fundamentals. Tonight is the first time management speaks publicly since the FT report five weeks ago, and the price implies essentially zero deal probability - if the market carried even a 20-25% chance of a >$3bn takeout the stock would not be trading below where it stood before anyone had heard of the bid. That makes the left tail self-limiting (a cheaper price makes the deal easier for a strategic acquirer who has never denied being at the table) and leaves a fat, unpriced right tail if the answer to the inevitable Q&A question is anything other than 'no comment'. If it were priced there would be a visible arb spread, a bid-supported floor and elevated call open interest; instead front-expiry total open interest is 5,641 contracts with a 2.14 put/call ratio and a 69%-of-mid ATM spread.
findings.independence: The idiosyncratic-vs-index decomposition rests on two separate price series I pulled independently: AMBA daily closes ($69.19 on 2026-07-29, $86.00 on 2026-07-31, $81.85 on 2026-08-05) at https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/amba/history/ and SOXX daily closes (530.70 on 2026-08-05, 494.40 on 2026-09-03) at https://stockanalysis.com/etf/soxx/history/. The absence of any collapse report is itself corroborated by the most recent dated deal coverage still describing talks as merely ongoing and unconfirmed as of 2026-08-13 - https://www.remio.ai/post/nxp-reportedly-explores-ambarella-acquisition-but-the-edge-ai-deal-remains-uncon

searched_and_found_nothing: Any report that the NXP talks were confirmed, abandoned or stalled - searched Reuters/Bloomberg/FT framings repeatedly; the newest dated coverage is 2026-08-13 and still says only 'ongoing, not certain'. Neither company has ever commented.

Arashi Vision (Insta360, 688775.SS), a named Ambarella action-camera customer, published H1 2026 on 2026-08-27: revenue RMB5.52bn +50.29% yoy but a RMB94.3m net loss and R&D +79.26%. Backing out Q1's RMB2.481bn gives Q2 of ~RMB3.04bn, +22% QoQ - not obviously inconsistent with Ambarella's $105-111m guide, so no directional read. https://www.guandian.cn/m/show/593103 . Their stated push into self-designed custom chipsets is a multi-year threat, not a print event.

GoPro v Insta360 ITC exclusion order - real but dated 2026-02-26 and limited to legacy Ace-series models not currently sold in the US, so no read on the May-July quarter. https://petapixel.com/2026/02/27/us-itc-rules-insta360-did-not-infringe-gopros-utility-patents/
Ambarella's careers page (ambarella.com/careers) resolves to a portal login with no public postings, so no team-level hiring or headcount signal was obtainable.

No Form 4 or Rule 144 filings since 2026-07-10 despite three of each in the first ten days of July - looked like an MNPI blackout tied to the deal, but it is fully explained by a routine pre-earnings blackout ahead of the 31-Jul quarter end. Discarded as a non-signal.

Ambarella's own 'Industry Analyst Briefing Call' (inaugural 2026-06-04, quarterly thereafter) is invitation-only with no webcast or replay, so its content - which would have been an uncovered public-ish channel - cannot be obtained.

Zero Ambarella business press releases between 2026-05-28 and the 2026-08-11 earnings-date notice; a >10-week silence is suggestive of a live sale process but too weak and too easily explained by summer to size.
The one clearly idiosyncratic session, 2026-08-17 (AMBA -4.27% while SOXX +1.58%), has no attributable news I could find.

WT Microelectronics is 61% of revenue and publishes monthly Taiwanese revenue, but it is a multi-billion-dollar broadline distributor and Ambarella is far too small a share of it for the monthly print to carry signal.

The Hanwha long-term edge AI agreement turned out to be dated 2026-05-28, announced alongside Q1 results (not late June as secondary coverage claimed) - so it is inside the last guidance and fully priced; the +28% day on 2026-06-30 was a Rosenblatt H2 top-pick note, not news.
baseline_tension: My main finding cuts WITH the run-up and the 2.14 put/call ratio, which is the weak position to be in on a name already 31.5% off its high - so I have deliberately kept it small and leaned on the fact that the -20% slide is attributable to a merger-premium unwind and the SOXX tape rather than to anything fundamental, leaving the wafer-commitment contraction genuinely unspent; against that, the erased takeover premium and the 5,641-contract front-expiry open interest argue the left tail is thinner than the -9.2% mean of seven prior reactions implies, which is why I land at -4.0 and not near the 14.4% implied move.
